items.title: Arrival & the Corniche at dusk
items.pace: Light — land, check in, one easy walk before dinner.
items.tldr: Land, settle in, and take the free Corniche walk to the Bock at golden hour before dinner in Clausen.
items.body:
Bus 16 or 29 from the airport into the centre is free and runs every 10–15 minutes — no need to plan around a taxi unless there's a lot of luggage.

Once settled, walk the Chemin de la Corniche toward the Bock promontory for the golden-hour view over the Alzette valley — free, no timing pressure, and a good way to get oriented before the fuller days ahead.

Dinner at Mousel's Cantine sits right at the bottom of the Bock, a short walk down. Friday dinner service fills up: call +352 27 67 23 42 or use its online form if you'll get there after 19:00, as this plan does.

items.title: Upper town — market, museums, fortifications
items.pace: Balanced — market and old town in the morning, the two museums split across midday and afternoon.
items.tldr: Saturday market, the old town's cathedral and palace, then MNHA and Fort Thüngen's Musée Dräi Eechelen.
items.body:
Start at the Place Guillaume II market (Wed & Sat only, 07:30–14:00) for coffee and a look at the produce stalls, then work through the old town on foot: Notre-Dame Cathedral, the Grand Ducal Palace (exterior — the interior only opens in summer), and the Fëschmaart square, home to the MNHA.

The market's food-stall village runs 10:30–14:00 and the MNHA is five minutes' walk from the square — loop back for lunch before the stalls pack up.

In the afternoon, cross toward Kirchberg for Fort Thüngen and the Musée Dräi Eechelen — buy the €12 combined ticket with MNHA if visiting both the same day.

Bock Casemates is about 20 minutes on foot back toward the old town, and makes a good end to the fortifications thread; last admission is 19:00, later than any of the day's museums. For dinner, Manzoku Ramen Bar is open this Saturday evening if a change from Luxembourgish food appeals.
constraints: Market runs Wed & Sat only — this is the one day it lines up with the trip

items.title: Vianden Castle, then down into the Grund
items.pace: One committed morning out of the city, one relaxed afternoon back in it.
items.tldr: A free train + bus out to Vianden Castle in the morning, then the Pfaffenthal lift down into the Grund for the afternoon.
items.body:
Take a CFL train to Ettelbrück, then RGTR bus 181 on to Vianden — both free, together under an hour each way. ⚠ Confirm the current bus 181 departure time on the mobiliteit.lu app that morning; the Ettelbrück hub was reorganized in May 2026. The castle is open 10:00–17:00 in October (last entry 16:30); budget about two hours there plus travel, aiming to be back in the city by early-to-mid afternoon.

Back in Luxembourg City, take the free Pfaffenthal panoramic lift down from Pescatore park into the Grund, and walk the valley floor along the Alzette — Neumünster Abbey's cloister garden is a natural stop — before riding the lift back up or finishing the loop on the Corniche.

Sunday thins the food options out: the market doesn't run, Oberweis and Manzoku are closed, and Mousel's Cantine serves only 12:00–16:00. Kaito Ramen by the central station runs until 21:30 every day, and is the dependable Sunday dinner.

plan_b.body: Neumünster Abbey's cultural centre (28 Rue Münster, in the Grund) has covered cloister and courtyard space and is open daily 10:00–18:00, free to enter — a dry fallback for the valley-walk half of the day if the weather turns. The Vianden Castle interior itself is indoors and unaffected by rain.

items.title: Villa Vauban & the Pétrusse valley, then departure
items.pace: Light morning built around what's actually open, then the airport.
items.tldr: A last museum that's actually open on a Monday, a walk in the Pétrusse valley, then a free bus back to the airport.
items.body:
MNHA and the Musée Dräi Eechelen are closed on Mondays, so this morning is Villa Vauban (open Mondays 10:00–18:00) instead, followed by a walk through the Pétrusse valley park just below the old town — shaded paths and old rampart views, no ticket needed.

Bus 16 or 29 back to Findel Airport is free and runs every 10–15 minutes; build in extra time if checking a bag or returning a rental.
constraints: MNHA and Musée Dräi Eechelen closed today — Villa Vauban stays open Mondays

title: Health & pharmacy
body:
112 is the emergency number for police, fire and ambulance, valid everywhere in Luxembourg.

Outside normal hours, a rotating pharmacie de garde (duty pharmacy) keeps at least one pharmacy open nationwide from 8am to 8am the next day. Current duty pharmacies are listed at pharmacie.lu and posted in every pharmacy's window; at night, ring the bell and present your needs through the hatch.

US travel insurance is worth arranging before you go — Luxembourg has no reciprocal healthcare agreement with the US, and Schengen entry technically expects proof of coverage.

title: Etiquette & language
body:
Three official languages share the country: Luxembourgish is the everyday spoken language, French dominates shops, menus and signage, and German shows up in print media. Around 80% of the population also speaks English, but opening with "Bonjour" rather than English is the local norm and is well received.

A brief handshake is the standard greeting, including in casual encounters with shopkeepers and waitstaff — cheek-kissing is reserved for people who already know each other. Luxembourgers tend toward reserved, polite phrasing over overt friendliness; it isn't coldness, just the register.

Punctuality is taken seriously for any timed booking or tour.
